description: We are 6bit_Larry, six CS undergraduates building Tour de Mars for NASA Space Apps 2026. Our team combines development, research, and QA to create MarsWalk, an EVA planner with interactive mapping, route comparison, and oxygen estimates. We use NASA Mars Trek imagery, support USGS CTX terrain data, and reference published Mars research.
summary: Tour de Mars is an interactive Mars exploration and mission-planning prototype designed to help future astronauts, researchers, and educators explore the Martian surface and plan science-focused Marswalks. Using real NASA/JPL Mars Trek imagery from HiRISE, CTX, and MOLA/HRSC, our platform provides an interactive map of Mars, focusing on Jezero Crater. Its terrain-planning system can process official USGS/NASA CTX elevation data to compare Fast, Safe, Balanced, and Science routes while estimating travel time, terrain exposure, and oxygen requirements. By combining authentic planetary observations with transparent mission-planning models, Tour de Mars makes Martian exploration more understandable, interactive, and accessible.
details:
Tour de Mars

An Interactive Martian Exploration and EVA Planning Platform

The Problem

Exploring Mars presents extraordinary challenges. Astronauts must navigate unfamiliar terrain, avoid dangerous slopes, identify scientifically valuable destinations, and manage limited life-support resources. Traditional planetary maps provide valuable observations, but astronauts also need an integrated tool that helps translate scientific data into practical mission-planning decisions.

Tour de Mars addresses NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge by developing an interactive prototype for planning surface exploration activities.

Our Solution

Tour de Mars is a web-based Martian exploration and EVA (Extravehicular Activity) planning platform. It brings together authentic orbital imagery, a terrain-processing system, interactive navigation, route comparisons, and mission-resource estimates.

Its central feature, MarsWalk, provides an interactive planning environment focused on Jezero Crater, the landing region of NASA's Perseverance rover.

1. Real NASA Mars Imagery

Our custom map interface connects to the NASA/JPL Mars Trek Web Map Tile Service (WMTS), using three map products:

  • HiRISE controlled Jezero mosaic: High-resolution surface imagery.
  • CTX controlled Jezero mosaic: Wider regional context.
  • MOLA/HRSC blended global imagery: Planetary-scale exploration.

These are genuine spacecraft-derived map products, not SI-generated or artificially created Martian terrain images.

2. Terrain Analysis and Decision Grid

MarsWalk supports the official USGS/NASA Mars 2020 Jezero CTX Digital Terrain Model.

When the elevation dataset is loaded, the system processes a 5 km × 5 km planning area into 2,500 cells of 100 m × 100 m.

The terrain-processing pipeline calculates elevation, slope, local relief, terrain costs, and passability indicators. These measurements support the route-planning system rather than relying on the visual appearance of satellite imagery.

The software also provides a clearly labeled illustrative rehearsal mode when verified terrain data is unavailable. Illustrative routes are not presented as validated terrain-safe navigation.

3. Four Route-Planning Modes

We developed four route-planning objectives:

  • Fast: Prioritizes reduced travel time.
  • Safe: Places greater emphasis on avoiding difficult terrain.
  • Balanced: Considers travel efficiency alongside modeled terrain risks and science context.
  • Science: Favors routes passing closer to selected scientific-interest waypoints.

The routing system uses a graph-based shortest-path algorithm with different cost weights for each objective. The science-interest layer currently uses contextual waypoints rather than measured CRISM mineral abundance.

4. Oxygen and Walkback Planning

MarsWalk includes an adjustable life-support scenario model that estimates oxygen consumption, remaining oxygen, travel time, and the reserve required to return to the base.

The system evaluates the modeled walkback oxygen margin along a proposed route and flags routes that violate the selected reserve assumptions.

These calculations are prototype planning estimates, not NASA-certified astronaut life-support limits or guarantees of mission safety.

5. Interactive Exploration and Scientific Context

Beyond MarsWalk, Tour de Mars includes a global Mars Atlas and scientific field notes covering Jezero Crater, Gale Crater, Olympus Mons, and Valles Marineris.

These sections explain the geological importance of major Martian destinations and connect users with NASA research, mission observations, and further scientific resources.

The interface also supports route comparison, route replay, inspection of mission points, and exporting planning information.

Technologies and Data

The project uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, NASA Mars Trek WMTS, GeoTIFF.js, and a custom graph-based route-planning engine.

Python, Rasterio, and NumPy support offline preprocessing of the official CTX elevation model.

Super Intelligence (SI) Usage and Transparency

Tour de Mars acknowledges the use of Super Intelligence (SI), including generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude, during project development.

SI assistance was used in four areas:

  1. Research and Information Gathering: Supporting the exploration of NASA scientific resources, technical documentation, and Martian exploration concepts.
  2. Data Analysis and Interpretation: Assisting with understanding terrain datasets, geospatial processing methods, and interpretation of modeled results.
  3. Coding, Debugging, and Troubleshooting: Assisting with JavaScript and Python development, code refinement, debugging, and troubleshooting.
  4. Writing and Editing: Supporting technical documentation, project descriptions, README content, and presentation materials.

Tour de Mars does not incorporate SI or machine-learning models into its operational route-planning engine. Its terrain analysis, route calculations, and oxygen estimates are implemented through conventional computational algorithms.

Code and Data Transparency: SI-assisted code and documentation are acknowledged in project descriptions and repository metadata. Original NASA/JPL and USGS scientific datasets are not SI-generated. Derived computational outputs are distinguished from source observations, and illustrative simulation data is labeled separately from verified terrain measurements.

The team retains responsibility for reviewing SI-assisted work, verifying scientific information, and making final implementation decisions.

Impact and Future Development

Tour de Mars demonstrates how planetary observations can become an understandable decision-support experience for human Mars exploration.

The prototype can support STEM education, mission-planning demonstrations, planetary science outreach, and future research into astronaut EVA planning.

Future development will focus on completing and validating terrain integration, incorporating additional scientific and environmental datasets such as THEMIS, CRISM, and MEDA, and improving route evaluation with mission-specific operational constraints.

Disclaimer: Tour de Mars is an educational and research prototype, not an operational astronaut navigation or life-support system. NASA-derived scientific datasets are distinguished from illustrative simulation outputs and SI-assisted development materials.
